So, I want to recommend this game. Because the first time I played it in 2020, it was fun. Played the first two maps (farm and dolls) with a friend and we had a blast! Then it was announced that a new map, The Woods map would come out in October 2020. Well fast forward 10 months and ton of delays later, and we finally get the update. Sadly it took nearly a year to make a level that is pretty much the same as every other level. Find items around the map, put them somewhere else in the map to weaken entity, then repeat 10 times. Yes it's technically a bigger map, and the concept could have been cool, but it was just over all lacking. And I think the thing that really stings is that it felt like we were promised so much and got so little. I guess if you're buying it as of today (07/25/2021) it's worth the 5 bucks because you get 3 somewhat fun levels. But I just hope if there is any future updates, that they aren't announced to far out in advance and/or we get actual updates as to why it's delayed and maybe some proof of progress. Idk, there still could be a great game in what's here, it just isn't one right now.

Pacify looks simple at first, but the moment the lights go out and you hear footsteps behind you, the game becomes pure panic. Played this with friends and half of the session was just screaming, running into walls, and blaming each other for getting caught.  The atmosphere is honestly the best part. The maps feel creepy without trying too hard, and the sound design keeps you constantly on edge. It’s one of those horror games where even opening a door feels stressful.  The gameplay can get repetitive after a while, and once you learn the AI patterns it loses some of the fear factor, but with friends it’s still ridiculously fun. Overall: 4/10  Pacify is a game that attempts to deliver a tense co-op horror experience but ultimately falls short due to its lackluster design and repetitive gameplay. The game has up to four co-op players, including you, working together to complete tasks while avoiding a relentless AI-controlled enemy, but this core mechanic quickly becomes more frustrating than frightening. To put it bluntly, none of the levels manage to offer an engaging or fun experience. Each environment feels uninspired, with objectives that grow tedious after just a few attempts on ANY of the missions. The atmosphere, while initially eerie, loses its impact as the jump scares and enemy behavior become predictable and honestly just monotonous. The game’s simplistic design leaves little room for strategy, reducing the co-op experience to frantic running and random item collection. Furthermore, the AI enemy usually feels more unfair than challenging, often resulting in irritating and unsatisfying encounters. Even at its low $5 price point, Pacify fails to justify its cost due to a complete and utter lack of meaningful content or compelling gameplay. Additionally, there are much better indie horror titles with MUCH better content around the same price point. This game may be fun to laugh at with your friends for half an hour, but for genuine horror fans seeking a deeper, more rewarding experience, this one is very hard to recommend...

However, the game quickly becomes tedious as you must repeatedly search the same areas for the same dolls, with the possessed girl randomly appearing to chase you down.  The AI of the possessed girl is poorly executed and easily exploitable, making it too easy to avoid her and cheapening any sense of danger or suspense. Furthermore, the game's jump scares are predictable and lacking in creativity.  Overall, I would not recommend Pacify to anyone looking for a satisfying horror experience. The game feels more like a cheap cash grab than a well-crafted game.

"A deceptively simple, highly stressful, and endlessly terrifying co-op nightmare."  Pacify proves that you don't need a massive AAA budget to scare the living daylights out of you and your friends. Set inside a creepy, abandoned house with a deeply unsettling backstory, the game gives you a simple goal: figure out what's going on, calm the possessed girl down, and get out alive. Easier said than done.  The atmosphere is pitch-black, claustrophobic, and dripping with dread. Every creak of the floorboards or sudden shift in the music means the little girl (or whatever she transforms into) is hunting you. Playing with friends turns into a chaotic symphony of screaming, laughing, and accidental betrayals as you try to coordinate carrying dolls, keys, and holy water while running for your life.  It's short, incredibly tense, and punches well above its weight class for an indie horror game.  Pros:  Terrifying atmosphere and brilliant use of psychological dread and jump scares  Perfect co-op game for screaming and laughing with friends  Simple rules that hide a surprisingly frantic and challenging gameplay loop  8/10 — Don't let her catch you, and definitely don't play in the dark alone.

Pacify is a paranormal horror game where you embark on four separate missions, each designed to capture unique and terrifying paranormal entities. Every mission features its own distinct environment, storyline, gameplay mechanics, and monsters, which keeps the game feeling fresh and engaging for a while. The combination of exploration, strategy, and jump scares makes it both fun and suspenseful, especially when played with friends.  That said, I have to give this game a negative review, though not in a completely bad way. The main reason is that Pacify can get a bit repetitive over time, which sometimes makes the gameplay feel boring after several missions. Additionally, the game lacks cross-platform play, so unfortunately you can’t play with friends who are on a console, which is a pretty big limitation for multiplayer-focused games. Despite these drawbacks, Pacify still offers a unique and enjoyable paranormal experience, and I can see it being really fun for short sessions or with a dedicated group of friends.

This is an amazing horror game with a dark, eerie atmosphere where you really need to know your way around. Some maps are very hard to finish in singleplayer, so it's recommended to find some friends to play with or join a random coop. I feel like that's how it's meant to be played. My two favorite maps are Dolls and The Wood. The rest is average, but still good in my opinion.  The first map is all about finding a way to solve the mystery at the abandoned mansion. I absolutely love this dark, abandoned mansion and running around chasing tiny dolls while avoiding the cursed girl. Here, it's crucial to memorize the the rooms and navigate between them flawlessly, because a single mistake means game over in solo mode. She can appear when you least expect it and make you a doll.  The second map, The Woods, is set far inside a deep, very old forest where a witch lives, and she is now the target. To defeat her, you need to complete a few steps and a ritual, because without it, she is practically immortal. Victory here requires a somewhat uncompromising approach and sharp shears. Planning what to do and in what order is the key.  The third map, Farm, offers a slightly different vibe, but it is still intensely dark and atmospheric. The monster is different and very hungry to eat anything on its way. The outdoor atmosphere is amazing, featuring a huge full moon and the creepy windmill. All of this gives the impression that we are far away from civilization.

The game places you and your teammates in a spooky environment where you must work together to survive and solve various terrifying puzzles. What makes it so much fun is the cooperative aspect—if you’ve got a group of friends, it’s an absolute blast, filled with tense moments, jumpscares, and plenty of laughs as you try to outsmart the creepy threats lurking around every corner.  The gameplay itself is straightforward but effective: explore, find items, solve puzzles, and try to keep the creepy entities at bay. The horror elements are well done, and the creepy atmosphere adds to the tension. While it’s not the scariest game out there, it does a good job of keeping you on edge. It’s also pretty accessible, so even if you’re not a hardcore horror gamer, you’ll still find it enjoyable.  Conclusion Pacify is a fun and intense horror co-op experience, and it’s definitely more enjoyable when you have friends by your side. The game’s solid mechanics, creepy atmosphere, and cooperative nature make it a worthwhile play if you’re looking for a good time with friends. Rating: 7/10

6/10  Pacify is a decent game that can bring laughs to you and your friends, but feels like there should be more.  Pacify is a game where you go into multiple situations trying to pacify entities and spirits to bring them to a secure prison facility. You "pacify" these entities by interacting with items around the map that will power them down. At first, starting off for your first time can be a little tricky since there isn't much to tell you what to do, so it starts as trial and error, but after you get the hang of it, you will know exactly what to do.   I recommend to play this game with friends since having multiple friends experience the same scary encounters is always a plus, but playing this game by yourself can feel pretty dull after a while. Each map has its own objectives but is pretty straight forward, always wanting you to do the exact same tasks on each one, every run. Like i said though, playing this with your friends and others is a big plus and brings this game up more for me, i just feel like this game doesn't have much for you to do in it.  Overall, Pacify is a fun experience if you want to play with others, but lacks in things to do if playing by yourself.
